title: The ring theorem: which knots remember a loop
claim: For links that are knots (forgetting reading) with one witness in, one witness out and any number of middle distinctions: (1) each transfer table of a knot link is a permutation (identity or swap) or misses at most one pair; (2) a ring excludes a middle pattern exactly when every transfer along it is a permutation and an odd number of them swap; (3) two middle patterns that differ in one middle distinction are never both excluded, so a ring composes into a knot or into nothing; (4) a knot link has only permutation transfers exactly when it is a parity relation; (5) a ring of k >= 1 copies of one link excludes some pattern exactly when the link has a swap table and either k is odd or the link also has an identity table. Statement (5) replaces the census prediction P3, which ticket A refuted.
failure_conditions: The kernel rejects the file, or a stated theorem depends on an axiom other than propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
A control that alters a statement (even instead of odd, a link that is not a knot, dropping the identity-table condition) is accepted.
The theorems disagree with the exact census KNOT-LOOPS-20261019-001A-E001 on its cases.
foundation_claim_scope: Which knots, joined in a ring through witness distinctions that are then forgotten, leave the ring constrained. No native recurrence, composed topology, path, metric, space or physical claim.

validation.status: checked: Lean 4.32.2 kernel accepted with standard axioms; four controls rejected; agreement with the exact census on 9,108 ring placements and 82,824 mixed rings; no human or external review
validation.level: V2 trusted kernel for statements 1-5; V1 census agreement; the counting formula argued in prose and confirmed by the census.
validation.novelty: known-overlap-likely: composing transfer tables is the transfer-matrix method, and parity rings are Tseitin contradictions on a cycle; the project's reading is new: among knots only permutation transfers carry a loop, and only parity carries it at full strength.
